anchor: RBI directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
argumentsAgainst: Repeated extensions can prolong uncertainty for depositors and members if a durable resolution is not achieved.
The extension itself does not establish that the bank's financial position has improved.
argumentsFor: The RBI stated that continuation was necessary in the public interest.
A time-bound extension subject to review allows regulatory oversight to continue while existing terms remain in force.
background: Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 is the statutory basis cited for the RBI's directions in this record.
Section 56 makes the cited Banking Regulation Act provisions applicable in relation to co-operative banks.
The record concerns Konark Urban Co-operative Bank Ltd., Ulhasnagar, and traces the directions to April 23, 2024.
indiaImplications: The case illustrates the RBI's regulatory role in safeguarding public interest in the co-operative banking segment.
Depositor confidence depends on clear communication that regulatory extension is not equivalent to confirmed financial strength.
A review-linked, time-bound approach can balance continuity of supervision with the need for eventual resolution.

officialFacts.text: The Reserve Bank of India, exercising powers under sub-section (1) of Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, extended the Directive for a further period of three months from close of business on October 23, 2026, to close of business on January 23, 2027, subject to review.
The RBI stated that the extension and/or modification of the Directive should not per se be construed to imply that it was satisfied with the financial position of the bank.
The RBI stated that other terms and conditions of the Directive under reference would remain unchanged.

The RBI had issued Directions to The Konark Urban Co-operative Bank Ltd., Ulhasnagar, under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, through a Directive dated April 23, 2024, initially for six months up to close of business on October 23, 2024.
The previous extension continued the Directive up to close of business on October 23, 2026, through a Directive dated July 15, 2026.

advisory_notes: "Section 56 makes the cited provisions applicable ... to co-operative banks" is broadly correct, but the exact statutory modifications are not detailed.
"Safeguarding public interest" is an analytical inference; the release states continuation was necessary in the public interest, not that the case proves effective safeguarding.
"Pursue a credible resolution pathway" is a reasonable recommendation, but the release does not state that any resolution process exists.
"Repeated extensions can prolong uncertainty" is a plausible implication, not an established consequence in this specific case.
"Depositor confidence depends on clear communication" is general analysis and should not be read as a source-established finding.
The headline, deck, paragraphs, applied-question answer, and hypothetical correctly distinguish continued directions from proof of financial soundness.
The proposed GS2.7 and GS3.1 tags are defensible for governance/regulation and banking-sector economic issues, though the precise numbering depends on the syllabus taxonomy used.
The source page is dated October 19, 2026; the note should avoid treating that future-dated record as current unless the examination context is after that date.
